text.tspan: From Learning Need to Readiness Decision
A new engineer moves through eight stages of orientation, demonstration, practice, support and first assignment, but the journey does not produce consistent evidence of independent-work readiness.
Engineering Manager explains the work need
Technical Trainer provides task guidance and feedback;
Is this a workflow issue, technical
Apply the workflow to standard work
New Engineer → Technical Trainer / Senior Specialist
Understand whether independent work is permitted
Trainer and Senior Specialist provide review input.
Where involved, the Learning or Competency Lead
and informal judgment; evidence remains inconsistent
Learning or Competency Lead where involved →
Materials are not organized by stage or task.
Advancement, completion and readiness expectations remain unclear.
Guidance, feedback and review depend on individual trainers or specialists.
Outputs are not compared against one common evidence threshold.
Unapproved or outdated guidance can remain active.
Informal readiness decision based on assignment output,
review comments and inconsistent supporting evidence.
Independent completion of standard technical work with
readiness that can be verified consistently.
Independent-work readiness cannot be verified consistently.
The learner journey does not create a controlled connection between learning activity, performance evidence and the final readiness decision.
Anonymized reconstruction based on professional experience. All proprietary names, data, interfaces and technical details have been replaced.
